svg.text: Mixture of Experts: How LLMs Scale to Trillions Without Slowing Down
Dense vs Sparse: The Core Idea
All 47B params active for every token - 47B FLOPs/token
Router selects top-k experts per token
47B total / 13B active = 3.6x less FLOPs per token
Where Experts Go: Replacing the FFN
Key: Only the FFN becomes sparse. Attention stays dense
and shared. Each expert is an independent SwiGLU MLP with its own weights.
Router: How Tokens Pick Their Experts
Example: Router scores for 8 experts (top-2 selected):
y = w1 * Expert5(x) + w2 * Expert1(x) (others skipped)
After training, experts self-organize into specialized roles.
Different tokens route to different experts automatically:
Untrained routers favor a few "winners" - other experts starve.
E0/E1 overtrained, E3/E4/E6/E7 never learn - wasted capacity
Add penalty pushing router toward uniform expert usage:
f_i = fraction to expert i, P_i = mean router prob for i
+ More params/knowledge without proportional compute - Higher VRAM (store all experts)
